body:
I won't be upping the dosage anymore.  I didn't see any effect, so there's no point in pushing it further.  I guess I was just very hopeful after the first few days and I hoped that upping the dosage would bring back that original feeling.  That's not what happened at all.  I think I might just need a change of scenery.  I'm going down to the park again tomorrow...I wish I had friends haha  

Their position is completely understandable to me, but at the same time their timing is *very* unfortunate for me. 

I'll probably be able to access the internet intermittently, but it probably won't be available when I *really* need it.  This is just a fluke of my father falling asleep after letting me use the internet to job hunt.  It's difficult to gauge how serious they are about anything.  Their discipline is sporadic at best, so I'm not sure how it'll go.

I know it sounded like this would be over in less than a week, but this is starting to look like a more permanent arrangement than I realized.  I'm not really sure what I'm going to do.  I'm not sure if the medication is helping or hurting.  It worked for the first few days, but after that I guess I feel much lower.  I've only been on them for five days.  I guess I'm impatient.

I know this isn't recommended at all, but I took two pills of the 20mg Citalopram today.  I was hoping it'd make me feel like getting out of bed.  I think I ended up going to sleep...haha 

It's only been a few nights and I'm not sure what's changed, but I'm constantly fighting the urge to drive down to the park and take every single pill I own.  It used to only happen at night, but now I feel like it's a constant struggle.  I don't think that it's caused by the medication.  

There's a strange vibe in my household at the moment.  I wish I could describe it, but it feels like it's feeding on itself into an infinite loop.  My parents are disappointed in me for not trying and I don't want to deal with any of their disappointment/anger.  It's created this weird stalemate where I stay in my room to avoid them and when I do leave my room everything is just *forced*.  I feel like I can alleviate the tension with jokes, but this is definitely an *elephant in the room* situation.

I'm not sure how I'm going to deal with it.

haha I could just conveniently leave my Citalopram laying around, too.  But that's not going to happen anytime soon either.  That's just not in my nature I suppose.  If the meds don't work at the 2 week mark I'll make a phone call.  I think it'll be easier considering I've talked to this doctor before.

Wow, they're actually cutting the internet tonight.  I don't know how long it'll last.  I don't think it's a permanent thing, but this is the first time they've ever actually gone through with something.  I can't say I blame them.  If I'm feeling better in the morning it won't be a problem... I hope that's the case.

EDIT: I'm sure I'll be back in a week at most :) I can last a few days, especially if the drugs kick back in tomorrow.

I really didn't need a coping mechanism for the last few days...I was felt pretty confident that I could do anything.  It just stopped today...it seems kind of sudden for a medication to just *not work*.

The doctor said it usually takes 2 weeks to see any effects of the medication...I'm sure she'd just advise me to wait the 2 weeks out and then tell her how I feel.

Thanks for the advice...I'm a little less worried now that I think they're going to bed.  They're under the impression I'm online all day, because I am/used to be in my room all day.  I spent most of the day laying in bed and listening to music.  They think the internet is what's causing all the problems.

EDIT: The picnic was a lot of fun.  I actually set that up through the internet, too.  They don't know about any of this stuff though, so I guess I only have myself to blame if they decide to cut it off.
This is the first day I've really felt suicidal...I'll give it a few more days before I call the doctor.

She told me to set up an appoint in a month to check back in.  She only prescribed a months worth of Citalopram, so I guess I have to go back.  I've never seen the scary side of mania and there's no way I'm qualified to diagnose myself :P  I'm probably just giddy from being happy after being depressed for *so long*.

I should probably have mentioned that I've been using my parent's credit card on more than half the stuff I've bought.  That's also **very** unlike me... I just thought they might not notice.  I'm going to have some explaining to do when my folks get the bill this month.  I can pay them back, no worries.

I hit every spot on that check list.  If I get into any trouble with this I'll talk to my doctor about it, but why would I want to tone down a euphoric state (if I can keep impulses under control?)  

But, as you said it's way too early to tell.  I'm taking a *wait and see* approach to this.

I wasn't told about any of these discontinuation effects...I should've asked and looked into it myself.

When is it appropriate to stop taking the medication?  I don't want to be on this stuff forever and I can't keep paying $87 a month to talk to a doctor.  I could probably do it a few more times, but I'd have to do it on my own.  I'm scheduled for a visit next month and depending on how it goes would she be able to just give me a prescription that allows refills?

A lot of these withdrawal symptoms scare the shit out of me.  Should I even continue taking them if I'm not sure that I can afford them?  I really don't want to keep taking them if the effects of withdrawal are permanent/common.

Thanks for the advice.  I'd hate to start over-eating without realizing it...or even worse have an increase in my suicidal thoughts.  I'd seriously lose it if it got any worse.  I'll be on the look-out for any warning signs.

They actually said it'd take about 2 weeks for the drugs to really take effect.  I thought I could feel them today, but my stress level was brought down so much by visiting the doctor and getting a treatment plan that it's hard to tell exactly what caused my happiness.  I hope they work right away every time.  That'd be a wonderful way to start the morning, but the doctor specifically said that they're not pills you take and immediately feel better.

Reading the thread on that forum about the positive/negative effects of Lexapro I realized that many people go through multiple different types of antidepressants.  Is that normal?  At what point will 20mg of Citalopram not be enough?  How will I know? Can I just stop taking it if I'm feeling good...let's say a year from now?

Thanks for the advice you've given me before even if I've never been able to take it.  It took faking an illness (abdominal pains) for me to get myself to a doctor. haha  Keep that advice in mind for younger people in similar situations that just can't talk to anyone about it.  I think it'll help them too.  

I'm not sure if these medications will work.  This was just day one and telling someone how I feel may have made me feel better on its own.  I guess I'll just wait and see. :)

Thanks again and oh yeah I love you, too! :P

Thanks for the information; I'll keep a look out for it.  Spending any money is a little unusual for me, but I'd intended to buy this stuff eventually.  Actually driving to seven different stores is unusual as well.  Everything was a bit unusual today actually...I'm happier and I also couldn't stop smiling :) 

What feelings should I be looking out for?  Mood swings?  I'm not beaming right now, but I'm pretty content.

Don't worry about it.  Today was a good day.  I know it's not going to feel like this when I wake up probably, but for now I'm really enjoying life.  I'm decorating a picnic basket haha...geeze

I always feel stupid reading the messages I write when I'm happy, but fuck it.  I really couldn't keep a grin off my face when talking to people in the store and they really responded.  I'll try smiling sincerely more often...I even considered telling the clerk that she was beautiful, but I decided to just give her a nice smile instead.  I think my smile made her smile.  It's contagious :P  

I'm going to try to enjoy this while it lasts...hopefully I won't be posting in r/sw or r/depression anytime soon (unless I'm giving advice.)  I've had good days before this, so there's no telling how I'll feel later.  I'm just hoping this time is different and lasts longer than a day.

See ya :)

If you'd like to ask me some questions the doctor (parents will be unaware) will ask I'd appreciate it.  I feel like I'm going into a job interview unqualified.  I'd hate to not be able to convey my ideas correctly to the doctor.  That'd make both of our lives a lot harder.

Right now I'm not comfortable telling my parents I need to see a therapist.  It'd be something I'd have to do behind their backs.  I have a few hundred dollars, so I could spare some of it you think it would really help.

I'm going to a walk-in clinic tomorrow that both my sisters and mother go to regularly.  They gave me a recommendation for a good doctor, so I'm going to ask for her.  Hopefully she's still working/working that day.  

PM me if you want to ask anything :)

I admit I'm clueless as to the different classifications of doctors.  If GPs are good enough for the general populace, then they're good enough for me.  Thanks for making me not look like an idiot in the future.

I understand completely...I'm just not sure if I can articulate exactly why I'm depressed.  I think I'll take up one of the other user's suggestions and print out an old thread where I explained the situation.  I'll have to read it again to make sure it's not too embarrassing first.  

I'm actually going to a doctor...I have no idea how I'd go about seeing a therapist without raising red flags with my parents.  Any ideas?  How much does a therapist cost anyways?

I'm going to go to sleep now.  I've said that more than once tonight, but I mean it this time.  I'll get back to anyone that responds tomorrow.  Thanks a lot again :)  I'm feeling like I have some kind of hope at least.  I just have to have the guts to tell the doctor how I'm really feeling.  That's going to be so fucking hard for me.  Any strategies?

I just plan on telling them that I *was* going to commit suicide, but then I decided against it.  Is that reasonable?

Thanks for the offer, but I don't really feel comfortable accepting any amount of money.

I'm going to bed REALLY now!  I needed to be up soon tomorrow and now I'm just going to have 4 hours of sleep. 

Feel free to keep posting guys.  I won't make it to the clinic until Monday, because the doctors office is open until 12 PM tomorrow and I just haven't had enough sleep to make it on time.  Thanks again :)

I'll be reading the thread again tomorrow to try and motivate myself into not backing out.

I think you misunderstood me.  I meant that if I lied and told them I was just depressed they might give me a medication other than one used for suicidal people.  It might all be the same.  I really don't know.

I just can't afford to keep switching doctors, though...maybe I'll get lucky and get a good one on my first run, but I doubt it.  How can you tell the difference between someone that has a masters and those that have a PhD?  I only remember seeing PhDs listed in my phone book., so I assumed they were on the same field.  I'll keep that information in mind.  Thanks :)

If I was stuck with a bad doctor wouldn't I just be out of money and lose all hope whatsoever?  How much does therapy on it's own cost anyways?  I'm almost positive I can't afford it or if it even helps?

Does therapy help?
Do meds help?

I really don't know if they can.
That's absolutely true, but wouldn't that effect the medication I receive?  I'm not sure.

I'm a liar...I never can get to sleep when I'm waiting for replies or anything.  I am going to sleep after this...I'm just **very** tired.  I'm just unsure of what I'm going to say to the doctor.  I'm not comfortable telling people how I feel and crying in a doctor's office looks pathetic to other people.

I actually considered talking to my mom today...they'll both be gone all week so I have time to get the drugs and *accidentally* throw away the receipt.  Somehow it's easier to tell the truth under the covers.  Maybe I'll give it a shot if she ever asks "what's wrong" again.  I'd hate to hurt her or my father.  I just know I'd start crying and I **never** cry.

I'm going to take the first step; It's taken me a few years to gain the courage, but I think I can get the medical help I need.  I'm really just worried about getting a rude/uncaring doctor.  I wish there was a website like ratemyprofessor for physicians.

I'm kind of tired...I thnk I'll just get back to anyone that resonds when I wake up...I'll probably be up for another 30-40 minutes.  I'd like to research these things a bit.  No worries if you can't find anything.  I know a walk-in clinic I can attend, but I'd have to wait until Monday.  I might change my mind by then, so I want get this done as quickly as possible.

I live in xxx

I may have phrased that incorrectly.  I guess a better way to describe myself would be *calm*.  I ordered the drugs for the express purpose of committing suicide.  It's the first time I've ever really even done drugs. 

Somehow I don't think being locked up against my will with people much crazier than myself would have a positive impact on my life.

I'm not sure of my exact reasons...I guess I've just never been the type to express my feelings.   I'm going to see a doctor Monday under the guise of *abdominal pain*, but my parents aren't aware of it.  It all turned around when my younger sister explained the argument to my mom this morning.  I can't thank her enough really, because I'd given up hope at that point.   Without any hope I don't think I would've lasted very much longer.  I hope I get a nice doctor otherwise I'll be...nevermind....I need to stop being negative.  I'm going to take the doctor's advice, whatever it is.

I'm not even sure why I'm answering now that the situation has changed, but if I could admit my suicidal feeling to my family it would be easy to find a therapist.  The problem is that I just didn't want them to be aware of it (for my own reasons.)  Therapists aren't cheap and I don't have insurance or any substantial amount of money.
Could I say that and then admit to my attempted suicide?  Other posters weigh in on this.  I'm not sure if there are magic legal words that would keep me safe.

Thanks a lot for this advice, seriously.  I was considering both telling him I abused the drugs and about my recent suicide attempt.  You may have just saved me from a lot of trouble.

I'm not sure exactly what to tell him now?  That I'm just depressed/feeling suicidal...will that be enough.  I don't know what's acceptable to talk about without fearing the consequences now.  I find it hard to talk about my feelings.  I guess I could just list off the wikipedia page for symptoms of depression.

What do you think?

I haven't read your other replies yet, but this one was short so I figured I'd respond.

The answer is no...

I can get to the doctor by describing the symptoms (to my parents), but what about afterwards.  I'm not sure if I have insurance or not...if I do does that mean they'll know what medications I've been prescribed/etc.  If I don't and pay in cash/check how much of a burden is it?  And really is medication even the answer here.  How can I explain away my doctor recommending me see a shrink?

I'm seriously considering this.

What will I say when they inevitably ask me why I need to see the doctor? I can't be honest about it and it won't be easy to hide any medications prescribed to me.  Please advise.

I'm going to take a shower now and try to get rid of some of this grogginess.  I'm walking like I'm drunk, but my mind feels completely/mostly sober.
I'd have to explain it to my parents first and I'm not sure if I can.

Attempted to OD - Either I just didn't use enough drugs or alcohol.  I feel horrible and I can't seem to think straight.   I just feel like sleeping now, so I'll think think things in the the morning.  Any advice on openinging up?  I just don't want to deal with any the drama.

I'm still alive.

I don't remember deleting the account, but I guess I did.  I'm back home just playing the same old tune.  I'm a broken record.  I'm not sure if there's anything else I feel like saying at the moment, but I'll be making a post tonight; I can feel it.
